title: Reference Points and Effort Provision

original_source.version_note: Pre-publication author manuscript matching title/authors and central contribution; exact final wording may differ.

central_claims: Raising rational earnings expectations increases real-effort provision, consistent with expectation-based reference points.

source_manifest.title: Reference Points and Effort Provision
source_manifest.finding: Original central claims were recorded before follow-up grading.

source_manifest.title: Camerer et al. Evaluating replicability of laboratory experiments in economics — Supplement, Tables S1–S2
source_manifest.finding: The preregistered independent comparison tests whether raising the expectations-based reference point increases real-effort earnings; replication N=318, original focal N=120, p=.160. The project only retested one selected result per paper.

source_manifest.title: The Limits of Expectations-Based Reference Dependence
source_manifest.finding: Reproduces selected fixed-payment comparative statics but finds failures under other probability/payment manipulations; shares original author Goette.

source_manifest.title: Wage Elasticities in Working and Volunteering: The Role of Reference Points in a Laboratory Study
source_manifest.finding: Exley and Terry extend the Abeler laboratory design to wages and charitable effort; low-wage workers exhibit targeting, while wage increases sharply reduce it.

research.summary: The larger 2016 focal replication was inconclusive (p=.160); later overlapping-author work reproduces some comparative statics but exposes boundaries. Independent work uses the design for new wage and volunteering results. Overall validation remains mixed.
